paper.title: AtlasVA: Self-Evolving Visual Skill Memory for Teacher-Free VLM Agents
paper.central_claim: AtlasVA stores reusable experience for VLM agents as a three-layer visual skill memory (spatial heatmaps, visual exemplars, symbolic text), evolves danger/affinity atlases teacher-free from trajectory statistics plus grid heuristics, and reuses them as potential-style dense shaping rewards for PPO; a 3B Qwen2.5-VL agent reaches 0.93 average success on Sokoban, FrozenLake, 3D navigation and PrimitiveSkill, above GPT-5 (0.69), o3 (0.71) and VAGEN (0.78), with each of memory, evolution and shaping contributing.

evidence.quote: we propose AtlasVA , a teacher-free visual skill memory framework that organizes memory into three complementary layers: spatial heatmaps, visual exemplars, and symbolic text skills
evidence.support_explanation: Central object: three-layer visual skill memory injected into the VLM prompt.

evidence.quote: AtlasVA further evolves danger and affinity atlases directly from trajectory statistics and lightweight grid heuristics, and reuses these self-evolving atlases as potential-based shaping rewards for reinforcement learning.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory evolved from rollouts and reused as RL reward: a context-and-weights coupled system.

evidence.quote: AtlasVA leverages this privileged representation exclusively during training to construct and evolve persistent spatial priors across episodes; the deployed VLM policy relies solely on visual inputs
evidence.support_explanation: Privileged simulator GridState (positions, obstacles, targets) drives atlas evolution and rewards during training.

evidence.quote: which computes topological features (e.g., BFS fields and corner traps) on-the-fly for the new layout
evidence.support_explanation: For unseen validation layouts the heuristic branch (BFS fields, corner traps) builds the maps at inference; how the layout is obtained without privileged state is not described.

evidence.quote: we extract topological features from the current layout, such as corner-like deadlock regions and Breadth-First Search distances to target objects
evidence.support_explanation: Static heuristic branch encodes goal-distance (BFS) and deadlock knowledge by hand.

evidence.quote: this privileged state access is strictly confined to the offline atlas evolution and reward computation pipeline during training
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim of train-only privilege.

evidence.quote: At evaluation time, the VLM policy does not receive any of these low-level states.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim; reconcile with E004 (maps for unseen layouts built on-the-fly) is left unresolved.

evidence.quote: This scheduling coefficient provides safe, cold-start exploration guided by static geometry in early stages, while smoothly transitioning to experience-driven refinement in later stages without risking catastrophic forgetting
evidence.support_explanation: Blend M_final=(1-beta_k)M_heuristic+beta_k M_stat with beta annealed 0->1; statistics are layout-position specific.

evidence.quote: the danger penalty acts as a heuristic safety constraint that intentionally alters the optimal policy to prioritize safe navigation over hazardous shortcuts
evidence.support_explanation: Danger term is non-potential and changes the optimum; affinity potential also changes over training (non-stationary), so policy-invariance of PBRS does not apply.

evidence.quote: To prevent information leakage, all memory components (heatmaps, exemplars, and text skills) are evolved exclusively using trajectories from the training environments, keeping validation sets strictly separated for zero-shot evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Declared train/validation separation for memory evolution.

evidence.quote: AtlasVA achieves state-of-the-art performance across all evaluated benchmarks with an average success rate of 0.93 (Table 2 ).
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result: 3B PPO-trained agent 0.93 vs GPT-5 0.69, o3 0.71, VAGEN 0.78.

Table 2 row: 1.00 on all five PrimitiveSkill tasks; single numbers, no seeds or intervals, per-cell episode counts not stated (many baseline cells are multiples of 1/8, suggesting about 8 episodes in some cells).
Strongest trained baseline (RL with sparse reward, no atlas memory/shaping); no baseline gets the same heuristic/BFS information.

evidence.quote: In addition to its standard tasks (Place, Stack, Drawer, and Align), we introduce a new Swap task, which requires the agent to exchange the positions of two cubes.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors add a new task on which AtlasVA is trained; baselines' Swap numbers come from unspecified protocol.

evidence.quote: The baseline, relying solely on textual rules (Layer 3), struggles to exceed a 0.25 success rate in the 2D Sokoban environment due to severe modality mismatch and sparse feedback.
evidence.support_explanation: The only 'text-centric memory' comparison is the authors' own L3-only variant; SkillRL/XSkill/ExpeL are not run, and whether the baseline gets dense shaping is unclear.

evidence.quote: Disabling off-policy updates (w/o Atlas Evolution) restricts the agent to static rules.
evidence.support_explanation: Atlas-evolution ablation; magnitudes appear only in Figure 5 (image, not in the pinned text).

evidence.quote: Removing the visual skill memory (VSM), atlas evolution, or dense reward shaping consistently degrades performance across all spatial benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Five-way component ablation exists but numerical values are not auditable from the text.

evidence.quote: we clarify that these symbolic rules do not require any proprietary Teacher LLM (e.g., GPT-4) to generate or summarize
evidence.support_explanation: Layer 3 is built from the environment rulebook, i.e. hand-authored static text, not learned from experience.

evidence.quote: L3 Text Text Principles & mistakes Per-episode summarization ## Learned Principles
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 says L3 is updated by per-episode summarization, App C.3 says it is static from the rulebook: inconsistent description of the text layer's update rule.

evidence.quote: Our implementation caps the pool at 6 exemplars, which it populates within the first 40 training steps
evidence.support_explanation: Bounded exemplar pool with FIFO eviction and DINOv2 retrieval; keyframe selection criterion ('inflection points') is described only qualitatively.

evidence.quote: We empirically found that tasks requiring high-precision, long-horizon coordinate manipulation (e.g., PrimitiveSkill) benefit from stronger visual guidance
evidence.support_explanation: lambda_danger/lambda_affinity tuned per environment (0.05 / 0.1 / 0.3) while memory hyperparameters are said to be shared; tuning data not stated.

evidence.quote: a stage-success delta is folded into the Affinity Gain for multi-step PrimitiveSkill manipulations
evidence.support_explanation: Task-specific shaping heuristics added for 3D navigation (rotation bonus) and PrimitiveSkill (stage success), i.e. hand-engineered rewards.

evidence.quote: We adopt Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct as the base vision-language model. AtlasVA is optimized via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE).
evidence.support_explanation: Weights are PPO-trained; gains conflate weight learning, shaping, and memory.

evidence.quote: Does visual skill memory enable a compact 3B-parameter VLM agent to surpass significantly larger proprietary models on spatially intensive tasks?
evidence.support_explanation: The RQ compares a task-trained, privileged-state-shaped 3B model with zero-shot proprietary models.

evidence.quote: Their common recipe is to summarize successful or failed trajectories into text, retrieve the relevant summaries for a new state, and then rely on a strong teacher model to refine the memory over time.
evidence.support_explanation: Author characterization of SkillRL/XSkill; teacher cost is asserted but never measured.

evidence.quote: A primary limitation is the projection of table-top 3D manipulation into 2.5D visual priors
evidence.support_explanation: Only stated limitation; privileged-state dependence, new-task generalization and cost are not discussed.

evidence.quote: In contrast, AtlasVA rapidly climbs to approximately 0.80 success within 140 training steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Only training-efficiency number (steps); no GPU-hours/wall-clock/token comparison.

evidence.quote: the capacity of the visual exemplar pool (3 positive and 3 negative cases), were kept consistent across all environments
evidence.support_explanation: Shared memory hyperparameters; fixed capacity, no learned utility-based retention.

evidence.quote: AtlasVA circumvents these bottlenecks by shifting online adaptation entirely to visual atlases, which evolve directly from trajectory statistics without requiring external teacher supervision.
evidence.support_explanation: Author positioning against SkillRL/XSkill/Reflexion/ExpeL/Mem0.

signatures.object: Visual skill memory used in the policy prompt: from text-only skill/summary memory to RGB danger/affinity heatmaps + exemplar frames + text rules; baseline = text-only (Layer 3) memory.
signatures.information: Training: privileged simulator GridState (positions, layout, targets) and rollout logs (terminal failure positions, successful paths), screenshots. Inference: RGB observation + rendered memory; unseen layouts get maps from the heuristic branch computed on the fly.
signatures.operation: EMA (alpha=0.85) of batch danger maps (terminal failure positions) and affinity maps (visit frequency on successful paths) blended with static BFS/corner heuristics via beta_k annealed 0->1; exemplar pool of inflection keyframes (3+/3-, DINOv2 retrieval, FIFO eviction); text skills from the rulebook.
signatures.output: Rendered heatmap images and exemplar frames injected as <image> tokens; updated atlas after each rollout batch.
signatures.conditions: Grid-like or grid-projectable spatial tasks with accessible simulator state at training time.
signatures.feedback: Trajectory success/failure statistics; sparse binary environment reward.
signatures.selection_rule: No admission gate: all batch statistics are EMA-blended; exemplars chosen as inflection frames and evicted FIFO; text pruning every 10 updates (criterion unspecified).
signatures.selection_data: Training environments only (validation layouts held out).
signatures.persistence: Atlas tensors, exemplar pool and text skills kept across training; frozen at validation.
signatures.later_use: Prompted at every step during training and evaluation; also defines shaping potential for PPO.
signatures.claimed_effect: Average success 0.93 vs 0.78 (VAGEN), faster convergence than text-only variant.
signatures.failure_boundary: Position-specific statistics do not transfer across layouts (heuristic branch must carry unseen layouts); 2.5D projection limit; privileged state dependence.

signatures.object: Reward function of the PPO policy (weights are trained): atlas-derived dense reward r_visual = lambda_d*r_danger + lambda_a*r_affinity (+ format penalty, task-specific bonuses).
signatures.information: Atlas values at consecutive positions p_t, p_{t+1} (privileged coordinates), sparse env reward.
signatures.operation: Affinity potential difference (BFS-based gradient) and non-potential danger penalty added to env reward; scaled per environment (0.05-0.3).
signatures.conditions: Spatial tasks where position and goal distance are known to the trainer.
signatures.feedback: Atlas (itself updated from the policy's rollouts).
signatures.persistence: Reward function is recomputed from the evolving atlas.
signatures.failure_boundary: Non-stationary potential voids PBRS invariance; danger term alters optimum by design.

gap.author_gap: Text-centric agent memory loses spatial structure, depends on proprietary teacher LLMs, and textual rewards give delayed, ungrounded feedback for spatial RL.
gap.checked_gap: A real modality-mismatch argument for spatial tasks, but (i) the two non-weight neighbours it targets (SkillRL, XSkill) are not run, so the residual vs the actual frontier is unmeasured; (ii) teacher cost is asserted, not measured; (iii) 'teacher-free' is achieved by hand-coded BFS/deadlock heuristics and privileged simulator state, which moves the dependence rather than removing it.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion -> ExpeL/Mem0 -> SkillRL (2026), XSkill (2026), VAGEN (2025, strongest trained baseline), PBRS (Ng 1999). Versions as cited; no neighbour full texts in this pack.
gap.residue: Whether the evolving statistics, rather than static heuristics + shaping, produce gains on unseen layouts.
gap.stakes: Spatial long-horizon VLM agents (Sokoban deadlocks, manipulation).
gap.method_response: Visual memory + heuristic/statistic atlas + dense shaping in one loop.
gap.remaining_gap: Perception-only deployment, cross-layout transfer of learned statistics, evolving non-grid tasks.
unresolved: SkillRL/XSkill are not available as pinned text and not run as baselines.
How layout-based maps are produced at evaluation time.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: harvest a dense reward from rollout-derived structure and train the policy on it. Domain: adapt context from rollouts, train weights on the same rollouts, re-adapt context for the updated model. Both = rollout statistics feed a weight update and a persistent artifact.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS card expects self-generated in-distribution signals and an isolating baseline; domain card expects typed lever jobs and a declared split. AtlasVA uses privileged heuristics and lacks the isolating control.

claims.text: A 3B AtlasVA agent attains 0.93 average success, above GPT-5 (0.69), o3 (0.71) and VAGEN (0.78).
claims.setting: Sokoban, FrozenLake, 3D Navigation, PrimitiveSkill (Place, Stack, Drawer, Align, Swap)
claims.baseline_control: Zero-shot proprietary/open VLMs; VAGEN (RL, sparse reward)
claims.selection_vs_test: Memory evolved on training environments; validation layouts held out
claims.result_denominator: Single numbers per cell; episode counts unstated; Swap introduced by authors
claims.allowed_conclusion: Task-trained, privileged-state-shaped 3B agent outperforms listed baselines in the authors' benchmark selection; attribution to visual memory unestablished.

claims.text: Each of VSM, atlas evolution and dense shaping contributes; atlas can be bootstrapped from raw statistics without teacher LLM.
claims.setting: Component ablations on all four benchmarks
claims.baseline_control: w/o VSM, w/o Heatmap, w/o Exemplar, w/o Atlas Evolution, w/o Dense Reward
claims.allowed_conclusion: Authors report consistent degradation; magnitudes and hence relative contributions not auditable; evolution's role on unseen layouts is unclear because statistics are layout-specific.

claims.text: Dense visual shaping accelerates convergence (0.80 success in 140 steps vs text-only baseline <=0.25).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Faster learning versus an under-specified text-only baseline; shaping vs memory not separated.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A PPO-trained 3B VLM whose prompt carries rollout-evolved danger/affinity heatmaps and exemplar frames and whose reward is shaped by the same atlas outperforms zero-shot larger VLMs and a sparse-reward RL baseline on the authors' four spatial benchmarks (author-reported, no uncertainty); the separate value of visual memory vs shaping vs hand-coded BFS/deadlock heuristics is not auditable.
unresolved: Test-time source of layout/BFS maps and information parity with baselines.
